title: db extra: install psycopg3 alongside psycopg2-binary, never as a replacement
answers: Why does the docker-build integration test or a container image fail with 'No module named psycopg' after installing mlflow[db]?
Which PostgreSQL driver packages does the mlflow db extra install?
Can I drop psycopg2-binary from the db extra and only keep psycopg3?
body:
Path: The `db` optional-dependency extra in pyproject.toml is what `pip install mlflow[db]` pulls in for SQL-backed tracking, registry and auth stores, and it is also what the docker-build image installs.
Rule: Keep both `psycopg2-binary` and `psycopg[binary]` in the `db` extra. psycopg2 serves SQLAlchemy versions below 2.1, where the bare postgresql:// scheme defaults to psycopg2, and psycopg3 serves SQLAlchemy 2.1+, where the default flips to psycopg3. Removing either one breaks one side of that version range.
Symptom: On SQLAlchemy 2.1, a PostgreSQL backend started from the db extra failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psycopg', and the docker-build integration test failed because its image installs this extra.
Constraints: Installing the driver does not change any URI; the scheme pinning in create_sqlalchemy_engine (mlflow/store/db/utils.py) is a separate rule. Dependency lockfile churn from this change is generated and not a pattern to copy.
applies: Dependency or extra changes to the `db` extra and any image or CI job that installs it.
says: Container images built with database support fail to connect to PostgreSQL backend stores.
Installing database extras results in missing driver errors when connecting to PostgreSQL.
Ensure database installation packages include PostgreSQL drivers for both older and newer environments.
Automated container builds fail during database initialization due to missing PostgreSQL libraries.
search: The db optional-dependency extra in pyproject.toml must retain both psycopg2-binary and psycopg[binary] dependencies rather than replacing one with the other. This dual-driver requirement ensures compatibility across SQLAlchemy versions, where versions below 2.1 default bare postgresql:// URIs to psycopg2 and SQLAlchemy 2.1+ defaults to psycopg3. Omitting psycopg[binary] causes ModuleNotFoundError for 'psycopg' on SQLAlchemy 2.1 during PostgreSQL backend startup and breaks docker-build container images. This rule governs dependency packaging for SQL stores and container images without modifying runtime URI scheme pinning or lockfile generation patterns.
